article.headline: US and Iran Sign Memorandum of Understanding to End War
article.summary: The US and Iranian presidents have signed a deal aiming to end the war between the two countries, with the agreement calling for Tehran to dilute its stockpile of highly enriched uranium and waiving US-backed sanctions. The memorandum of understanding was signed by US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with the Pakistani PM stating that the deal takes immediate effect. The agreement has been met with varying reactions, with some countries welcoming the move and others expressing concerns.

The US and Iran have been engaged in a long-standing conflict, with tensions escalating in recent years. The signing of the memorandum of understanding marks a significant development in the relationship between the two countries. According to the BBC, the agreement aims to end the war between the US and Iran, with the Iranian president stating that the deal is a significant step towards peace. The memorandum of understanding was signed after months of negotiations between the two countries, with the US and Iran agreeing to work towards a peaceful resolution.

The agreement calls for Iran to dilute its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, which has been a major point of contention between the two countries. The waiver of US-backed sanctions is also a significant aspect of the agreement, with Iran having faced severe economic sanctions in recent years.
